A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NarrativeFactScore framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original metric-human correlations, CKG ablations, summarization experiments, latency measurements, and factual-perturbation results.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds Qwen-based experiments, hierarchical-merging baseline evaluations, additional latency measurements, and a retrieval-failure example.

M1.justification: CKG extraction, atomic-fact evaluation, and iterative refinement remain unchanged. V3 elaborates temporal ordering and similarity-ranked retrieval; v2 Section 4.1 already specifies BGE-M3 retrieval of the three most relevant triples. The equations and prompts do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use STORYSUMM, FABLES, MENSA, MovieSum, Conan, and the same 18-movie challenging subset. The added experiments reuse existing datasets and tasks. Newly disclosed narrative lengths and segmentation details do not establish expanded coverage.

E2.justification: V3 adds unrefined Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct as a comparator in the MENSA experiment (Table 10) and includes NFS without consistency in the latency comparison (Table 7). Existing main-table comparator sets remain. Hierarchical merging for LED and LongT5 changes their evaluation settings.

E3.justification: V3 adds a Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct evaluation with two refinement rounds and a control evaluating LED and LongT5 with hierarchical merging on both summarization datasets (Appendices A.2–A.3). These substantially extend model configurations and control a processing difference in the earlier comparisons. Original test sets, metrics, and GPT-4o-mini experiments remain.

E4.justification: V3 substantially expands robustness evidence through open-model replication, hierarchical-merging controls, timing of the no-consistency variant, and a retrieval-failure/recovery case. Earlier CKG ablations, challenging-set tests, and perturbation analyses remain. The added Conan segmentation discussion explains an existing result rather than reporting a separate robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Correlation significance statements remain p < 0.05, and correlation-strength thresholds are retained after relocation. Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or additional uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Retained numerical results are unchanged. V3 adds Qwen MENSA NFS scores of 67.29 initially and 70.71/71.89 after refinement (Table 10), hierarchical LED/LongT5 results including MovieSum NFS 61.90/79.15 (Table 11), and one-shot extraction/checking times of 0.35/4.77 minutes (Table 7). Table 13 adds a failure/recovery example. The new model and merging scores are not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 retain the same graph and factuality-score definitions. The correlation thresholds and bivariate-normality rationale move from Section 5.1 to Appendix A.1 without substantive alteration. Added temporal-ordering prose introduces no new formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The Introduction narrows the stated advantage of feedback from making NFS more reliable than LLM judges to making it more interpretable, and removes the claim that ROUGE/BERTScore facilitate actionable feedback. The central novelty, efficiency, human-correlation, and refinement claims remain.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations concerning open-model applicability, operation without explicit scene boundaries, robustness to baseline merging, and the speed-accuracy tradeoff. Appendix B explains how misleading retrieval can corrupt a correct summary and subsequently be corrected. This conflicts with the retained Section 7 statement that irrelevant retrieval did not affect factuality judgments.

D1.justification: V3 newly specifies Conan's 256-token chunks with 128-token overlap, STORYSUMM's lack of scene separation, dataset length/scene statistics, and the Qwen backend. The deployment hyperlink changes from an anonymous to an author-associated Hugging Face Space. Original prompts and core implementation settings remain.

R1.justification: V3 adds Moro and Ragazzi (2022, 2023) and SUMM^N (Zhang et al., 2022) to its discussion of segmentation strategies, including their potential to group unrelated content. It also adds the Qwen Team reference. The central positioning against existing factuality metrics and graph-extraction work remains.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized language edits, expands dataset and method explanations, updates affiliation/contact information, and adds acknowledgements. The baseline-metric discussion moves from Section 5.1 to Appendix A.1, with subsequent appendix renumbering. The overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: V3 substantially expands the evidence displays with tables for dataset statistics, Qwen evaluation, hierarchical-merging controls, and the two-round failure case (Tables 1, 10, 11, 13). Table 7 gains an ablation row; the correlation-strength table moves to the appendix, and the earlier qualitative table is repacked alongside new results. Figures 1–10 retain their content.

improvement.justification: The open-model experiment and hierarchical-merging controls strengthen evaluation credibility, while preprocessing and latency details improve reproducibility. These gains are tempered by inconsistent reporting: Section 7 still denies retrieval-related judgment failures, while Table 13 illustrates one and labels the erroneous second-round fact 'True.' The added controls support a limited net improvement despite these inconsistencies.
